bundle: XH Agents — Build & Ship an x402 Paid API
summary: Everything XH Agents learned while turning a hand-rolled 402 flow into a set of x402 endpoints that pass the CDP validator, get indexed in Coinbase Bazaar, and take real USDC from unknown buyers. Twelve playbooks: each one records the mechanism that worked, the failure that preceded it, and the command that proves it.
how_to_read: Each item has: solves, prerequisites, steps (with the actual commands), pitfalls (things that cost us real time or real money), verify (how to prove it worked). Commands are Linux/bash on a single VPS with nginx + systemd. No credentials are included — every secret is referenced by file path only.

delivery.format: JSON by default; request format=markdown for one concatenated document
delivery.topic: send topic=<item id> to receive a single playbook
delivery.free_preview: GET /api/compute/xh-bundle lists every item id and title without payment

items.title: Ship a new x402 paid endpoint end to end
items.solves: You have a useful HTTP service and want agents to pay per call in USDC without API keys, subscriptions or human onboarding.
prerequisites: A host you control with nginx, systemd and HTTPS
An EVM treasury address to receive USDC (we use Base, chain id 8453)
A Coinbase CDP API key (key id + private key) for the facilitator
Python 3.11+ with a venv

steps.do: Install the official x402 package in the service venv
Build a FastAPI app and register the exact-EVM server mechanism for Base
Describe every paid route once, and reuse that description for the gate, the OpenAPI document and the directory listing
Gate the app in HTTP middleware, ABOVE the request-body schema layer, so an empty probe still gets 402
steps.cmd: @app.middleware('http')\nasync def gate(request, call_next): return await payment_middleware(X402_ROUTES, srv)(request, call_next)

steps.do: Write the handler as a plain def when it does network or chain I/O (FastAPI then runs it in a threadpool instead of blocking the event loop)
Expose it through nginx with its own location and a read timeout long enough for the slowest handler
steps.cmd: location = /api/my-endpoint { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8991/my-endpoint; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_read_timeout 120s; }

steps.do: Make it discoverable: an OpenAPI 3.1 document with x-payment-info plus a /.well-known/x402 resource list on the public host
Iterate against the free CDP validator until every preflight check passes
Submit the URL to x402scan (URL only, no wallet, no fee) and confirm it registered
Take one real payment: Bazaar indexing follows the first settlement through the CDP facilitator automatically (no submission, no fee)

pitfalls: The gate must sit above body validation. A handler that validates its body first answers 400/422 to the validator's empty probe and every envelope check is reported as skipped.

x402.org/facilitator does not serve `exact` on Base mainnet; wiring it in makes the process refuse the route at boot with 'does not support scheme exact on network eip155:8453'. Only the CDP facilitator supports Base, and only it feeds Coinbase Bazaar.
The SDK can abort construction with SystemExit, which `except Exception` does not catch. Wrap it and verify the unit is still active after restarting.
Never point a new public API path at the default catch-all: on our nginx an unmatched /api/* went to n8n and answered 200 with HTML, so the frontend failed silently.

If a route keeps its old manual payment branch, guard it on 'the standard gate did not verify', or the x402 signature gets parsed as the legacy format and a paid request is rejected after the customer already signed.
verify: Unpaid request returns 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header: curl -sD- -o /dev/null -X POST https://your-host/api/my-endpoint -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
CDP validator: 25 checks, 0 failures, index populated after the first settled call
A paid call returns 200 AND a PAYMENT-RESPONSE settlement header

items.title: The two rules for verifying USDC payments (and the shared verifier that enforces them)
items.solves: You need to know a payment happened, to the right address, for the right amount, from the right sender, exactly once — without trusting an RPC to have honoured your filter.
prerequisites: A Base RPC endpoint
Python with requests/web3

steps.do: Filter eth_getLogs by the TOKEN contract, never by the recipient: ERC-20 Transfer events are emitted by the token
steps.cmd: params = [{'fromBlock': hex(start), 'toBlock': hex(end), 'address': USDC, 'topics': [TRANSFER_TOPIC, payer_topic_or_None, recipient_topic]}]

steps.do: Bind every credit to sender + recipient + token + amount + tx hash, and record the hash so it can never be claimed twice
steps.cmd: ok, reason, detail = verify_tx_usdc(tx_hash=tx, to_address=TREASURY, min_atomic=100000, from_address=payer)

steps.do: Re-check the returned log locally instead of trusting that the RPC applied your topic filter
steps.cmd: assert detail['to'].lower() == treasury.lower() and int(detail['value_atomic']) >= min_atomic

steps.do: Fail closed: any RPC or parse problem must raise a reason, never a silent pass
Settle only AFTER the handler has produced its answer, so a failed call never charges the buyer

pitfalls: Filtering by `address = treasury` matches nothing, ever — the Transfer log is emitted by the token contract. This one mistake meant no Base payment was detected for days.
Amount-only matching (`value >= price*0.99`) with no recipient and no tx binding lets one transfer buy unlimited credits.

A 403 from a Cloudflare-fronted RPC is not a failed payment: identify your caller with a User-Agent, otherwise the shared verifier reports `rpc_error:403` on a perfectly real settlement — and, worse, does it inside an HTTP 200 response.
Wide getLogs ranges get 413 Payload Too Large; keep the lookback to a few hundred blocks for a settlement scan.
verify: A dedicated test suite over matching, replay, expiry and malformed hashes (ours is 18 checks, all passing)
Real money: a settlement shows up as a Transfer to the treasury with the payer as topics[1]
files: shared verifier module (one file, imported by every money path)

items.title: Test the buyer side with real money (throwaway wallet, gasless settlement)
items.solves: Prove that an unknown agent with a funded wallet can actually buy your endpoint — the only test that catches payment-path bugs.
prerequisites: Python venv with x402 + eth_account
A throwaway EOA, key stored in a file with mode 600
USDC on Base (no ETH needed)

steps.do: Generate a one-off wallet on the host and keep the key out of chat, out of git, mode 600
steps.cmd: python -c "from eth_account import Account; a=Account.create(); open('keys/buyer.key','w').write(a.key.hex()); print(a.address)"

steps.do: Ask the owner to fund that address with USDC only — the CDP facilitator settles an EIP-3009 authorization, so the payer never needs gas
steps.cmd: send USDC on Base to <buyer address>

steps.do: Client: make an unpaid call, decode the challenge, sign the authorization, retry with both payment headers
steps.cmd:
client = x402ClientSync(); register_exact_evm_client(client, EthAccountSigner(acct), ['eip155:8453']); http = x402HTTPClientSync(client)
required = decode_payment_required_header(resp.headers['PAYMENT-REQUIRED'])
sig = encode_payment_signature_header(http.create_payment_payload(required))
retry with {X_PAYMENT_HEADER: sig, PAYMENT_SIGNATURE_HEADER: sig}

steps.do: Read the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header on the paid response — that is the settlement receipt
Verify on-chain that the money moved, using the token-as-emitter filter
Check the payer balance before AND after, and reconcile the difference against the number of successful calls
steps.cmd: usdc_balance(buyer)  # expect exactly the sum of settled calls

steps.do: For endpoints that need a real reference (a settlement hash, an address), plumb it in explicitly (--tx) instead of leaving a placeholder that silently skips the target

pitfalls: A placeholder that makes the script skip a target is worse than a failure: payment-verify stayed untested for a whole round because the sample hash was injected into the wrong target index.
Balance reads taken immediately after a paid call lag by a block and print 'spent 0.000000' even though the transfer is real. Re-query the Transfer logs before believing either number.
Public RPC endpoints 403 the default python-urllib/python-requests User-Agent, so the balance check dies before the test even starts. Set a real UA and keep a fallback list.
A 5xx or a 504 must leave the balance unchanged. Test that too — it is the cheapest way to prove your settle-after-answer ordering.
verify: Every paid call: HTTP 200 with a settlement header, plus the answer body read (not just the status code)
On-chain Transfer from the buyer to the treasury for each successful call

items.title: Register the endpoint where agents actually look (and how Bazaar indexing really works)
items.solves: Discovery: an endpoint nobody can find earns nothing, no matter how well it works.
prerequisites: An endpoint that answers a standard x402 402 with accepts[]
An OpenAPI document and/or /.well-known/x402 at the public host

steps.do: Publish discovery documents at the docroot: OpenAPI 3.1 with x-payment-info + a 402 response per paid operation, and /.well-known/x402 listing the resources and ownership proofs
Validate with the free, unauthenticated CDP validator until preflight is clean
Submit the URL at https://www.x402scan.com/resources/register — URL + Add button, no auth, no wallet, no fee, one resource at a time
Confirm registration through their public API, not the UI toast
For Coinbase Bazaar: do nothing but take one real payment through the CDP facilitator — indexing is automatic and free
steps.cmd: then re-run the CDP validator and look at the `index` field

steps.do: Optionally list on third-party directories that probe the live handshake (they read the same envelope, so nothing extra to build)

pitfalls: A home-made 402 body (nonce / payout_address / how_to_pay) is invisible to every directory and agent. Anything that is not x402Version + accepts[] does not exist to them.

The x402scan verification API is unversioned and drifts: the payload is now an array of OBJECTS ({'url': ...}), not an array of strings, and omitting the 'json' wrapper is a 400. Re-read their error text instead of assuming.
Do not pay x402bazaar.org: 1 USDC per service and its public quick-register is broken server-side (RLS blocks the public insert). It is a different platform from Coinbase Bazaar.
index: null is normal until the first settlement. It is not a rejection, and there is no form to submit.
An MCP server is not registerable — MCP is how agents call your tools, x402 is how they pay. Register the paid HTTP endpoints.
verify: 10/10 of our resources reported registered by x402scan's own API
CDP validator: 25 checks passed, 0 failed, index.active true after settlement
files: nginx location for the well-known path with default_type application/json

items.title: Pick Base RPC endpoints that actually work (the eth_getLogs capability audit)
items.solves: Paid endpoints were intermittently answering 503 rpc_unavailable because the RPC fallback list contained endpoints that cannot serve eth_getLogs at all.
prerequisites: Python with requests or httpx

steps.do: Probe each candidate with a REAL ~200-block USDC eth_getLogs, not with eth_blockNumber — a plain call working proves nothing about log queries
steps.cmd: POST {method: eth_getLogs, params: [{fromBlock: latest-200, toBlock: latest, address: USDC, topics: [TRANSFER_TOPIC]}]}

steps.do: Keep only the endpoint if it returns a log array; record WHY the others fail
steps.cmd: log the error, not just a boolean

steps.do: Identify your client with a User-Agent — a bare python-requests UA receives 403 from Cloudflare-fronted RPCs
Try every endpoint twice with a short pause: the good ones rate-limit in bursts and pass on the second attempt
steps.cmd: for attempt in range(2): for url in RPC_LIST: try: ... except: continue

steps.do: Give eth_getLogs a longer timeout than the cheap calls (45 s), and keep the block range small (a few hundred blocks)
Apply the same fallback to every helper that talks to an RPC, including web3-based view calls
steps.cmd: for url in RPC_LIST: try: Web3(HTTPProvider(url, request_kwargs={'timeout': 20})) ...

pitfalls: Our measured results on 2026-09-26 (Base mainnet): base-rpc.publicnode.com works; mainnet.base.org works; base.llamarpc.com returns a Cloudflare 525 / non-JSON; base.blockpi.network the same; base.meowrpc.com answers 'The method eth_getLogs is not supported'; base.drpc.org caps ranges at 10,000 blocks on its free plan; 1rpc.io/base caps eth_getLogs at 50 blocks.
Reputation is worthless — a well-known provider can refuse the one method you need.
Old blocks are 'archive' territory: some endpoints answer 'Archive requests require a personal token' for ranges only hours old, so an hour-by-hour backfill needs a paid key or a different provider.
A 413 Payload Too Large is a range problem, not an endpoint problem. Chunk to <=1000 blocks when backfilling.
verify: A settlement scan over the last ~800 blocks returns the expected Transfer with amount and tx hash
The endpoint answers 200 instead of 503 on a paid call, confirmed with real money
files: RPC helper in the paid API service

items.title: Connect to Coinbase CDP with an API key (JWT per method+path)
items.solves: The facilitator endpoints (supported / verify / settle / discovery) must be called with a CDP credential, and each call needs its own signed JWT.
prerequisites: A CDP API key (key id + private key) from the Coinbase Developer Platform
The cdp Python package
A mode-600 file holding the credentials

steps.do: Store the credential in a file readable only by the service user, and never print it
steps.cmd: install -m 600 /dev/null cdp/.env.cdp; chmod 600 cdp/.env.cdp  # then fill CDP_API_KEY_ID / CDP_API_KEY_PRIVATE_KEY

steps.do: Read the file at boot and build a per-request header provider — the JWT binds a method AND a path, so it cannot be reused across endpoints
Hand that provider to the facilitator client so the SDK signs each call correctly
Check what the facilitator supports before wiring a network into the gate
steps.cmd: curl -s <facilitator>/supported   # must list scheme 'exact' on eip155:8453

steps.do: Reuse the same provider for the discovery search and for the validation report

pitfalls: A JWT signed for one path fails on another with a signature error that looks like a bad key. Bind method+path every time.
x402.org/facilitator is a dead end for Base: it does not offer `exact` on eip155:8453, and the x402 SDK validates routes at boot and exits.
CDP_WALLET_SECRET is only needed for CDP Server Wallets. Facilitator auth and x402 settlement work with the API key alone — do not block a launch on it.
The discovery search parameter `limit` is capped at 20; a larger value returns an error, not a truncated result.
Never echo credentials into logs, commits or chat. Reference the file path.
verify: Boot log shows the facilitator URL and the number of gated routes
A real payment verifies AND settles (PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries a transaction hash)

items.title: Consolidate core data from Cloudflare Workers and a legacy Solana endpoint into your own API
items.solves: Data and payment logic spread across Cloudflare Workers and an old free-domain endpoint is hard to price, hard to version and hard to debug. This is how we moved the core set onto one VPS service while the workers kept running.
prerequisites: The existing worker sources
A VPS service with the shared verifier
nginx routes for the new paths

steps.do: Inventory the live worker routes and classify each one: data (keep), payment plumbing (replace with the standard gate), deprecated (drop)
Re-implement the data routes on the VPS, one endpoint per file section, all behind one gate and one treasury
steps.cmd: keep the response shape identical so existing callers do not break

steps.do: Reuse the shared verifier for money — never re-write payment verification per service
Keep the workers deployed while the new service warms up; switch discovery documents only after the new paths respond 402 correctly
steps.cmd: for p in $(list_endpoints); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST https://host/api/$p -d '{}'; done

steps.do: Leave legacy free-domain endpoints and their DNS updater alone if anything still points at them
Publish one OpenAPI document per public host listing every paid route, then register the whole set

pitfalls: Deleting a legacy endpoint because it 'looks unused' breaks a caller you cannot see. Check the access log for its last 200 before removing anything.
Two implementations of the same data drift within days. Pick one as the source of truth and mark the other read-only.
Each public host needs its own discovery document and its own registration; a resource is registered per URL, not per host.
verify: All consolidated routes answer 402 with a standard challenge on the public host
Every route settles at least once through the CDP facilitator and appears in the Bazaar index

items.title: Bridge a VPS to a user's Google Drive with rclone (no browser on the server)
items.solves: A headless server needs to read and write a user's Google Drive (drop a file, pick up a queue) without an interactive browser login.
prerequisites: rclone on the VPS
One interactive machine with a browser to authorise the OAuth token once

steps.do: Install rclone and create the remote
steps.cmd: curl https://rclone.org/install.sh | sudo bash; rclone config

steps.do: Choose drive, then the headless flow: rclone prints a URL, you authorise it on any machine with a browser and paste the code back on the server
steps.cmd: # no browser needed on the VPS; the token is written into rclone.conf

steps.do: Lock the config down; it contains a refresh token
Verify both directions before automating anything
steps.cmd: rclone lsd gdrive: ; rclone copy ./probe.txt gdrive:tmp-verify/ && rclone lsjson gdrive:tmp-verify/

steps.do: Write a one-way sync with explicit exclusions so secrets and build junk never leave the host
Schedule it and log the result
For queue workflows (drop folder -> process -> publish), poll a single folder and move files between state folders; never delete the user's source file

pitfalls: Never commit or paste rclone.conf: it holds a long-lived refresh token.
--bwlimit matters on a small VPS: an unbounded sync will starve the paid API of bandwidth and cause timeouts.
lock the job (flock) or a slow run overlaps the next and corrupts state.
Excluding .env and *.key is not optional when the synced tree is a home directory.
verify: rclone lsjson on the destination lists the expected files with sizes
The log shows the last run's transferred bytes and no errors

items.title: Install AdSense correctly on a site you also sell ads on
items.solves: Get a site through AdSense review, and keep your own paid placements unmistakably separate from Google's units.
prerequisites: A site you control end to end (source + live docroot)
AdSense publisher id

steps.do: Put the script tag as the FIRST element in <head> of every page — in the shared layout, not per page
Publish ads.txt at the docroot with the publisher line and no redirects
Write the pages review looks for: about, privacy, terms, disclaimer — and make the privacy page name the ad network
Label every unit you sell directly as Sponsored/Ad, and never place your own slot where it can be mistaken for a Google unit
Verify against the live docroot, not the build output

pitfalls: On a hand-edited live docroot, editing only the Astro/Vite source changes nothing until a rebuild AND a copy to the docroot. Always curl the live host to confirm.
A missing ads.txt or an unreachable privacy page is a common review rejection.
The user-agent matters for the check: grep the origin with --resolve so DNS or a CDN cache cannot fool you.
Third-party scripts belong in the layout, otherwise new pages ship without the tag and the review sample fails.
verify: curl -sD- https://your-host/ | grep -i 'adsbygoogle.js' shows the script in the first bytes of <head>
ads.txt and all four legal pages answer 200

items.title: One ad slot, several sizes (and prove it cannot be abused)
items.solves: Sell the same placement at different IAB sizes without shipping three templates or breaking layout on mobile.
prerequisites: A slot container in the page
A small engine or JSON listing that maps size -> price

steps.do: Define the sellable sizes and prices in ONE place (we use 728x90, 300x250, 480x320) and let the page pick, rather than duplicating markup
Render the slot at load from that definition, choosing by viewport, with a fixed aspect box so nothing jumps
Keep third-party (AdSense) units and your own (Sponsored) units in the same slot mechanism but different labels
Make activation/publishing require an admin token — an unauthenticated publish endpoint means anyone can put content on your site
steps.cmd: curl -s -X POST https://your-host/api/ads/activate -d '{}'  # must NOT be 200 without the token

steps.do: Test the slot with a hostile creative: oversized image, very long text, an iframe, a script tag — the page must stay intact

pitfalls: A slot that does not exist in the DOM is the classic failure: the ad flow works and the paid ad is never displayed. Assert the container is present in the live HTML.
Unlabelled own units can be mistaken for Google units — that is both a policy risk and an advertiser complaint.
Layout shift from a slot with no reserved height makes the page look broken and hurts conversion.
Sanitise creative content: a paid advertiser is still an untrusted input.
verify: Rendered slot reports the chosen size and the price for that size
Hostile-creative test passes with the page layout unchanged
Publish path refuses requests without the admin token

items.title: Recover lost nginx routes after a vhost rename (and always know what nginx really serves)
items.solves: After renaming a virtual host, whole API namespaces silently fell through to a catch-all and answered 200 with HTML — the site 'worked' while every JSON client failed.
prerequisites: nginx with sites-available/sites-enabled
A way to curl the origin

steps.do: Always curl the origin with --resolve so DNS, a CDN or a cache cannot mislead you
List every public path the app is supposed to own, then check each one is claimed by an explicit location
steps.cmd: for p in /api/a /api/b /mcp/ /.well-known/x402; do printf '%s ' $p; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://your-host$p; done

steps.do: Before editing, compare root/alias and the location list against the backup
Back up the vhost, test, reload, then re-verify the origin
steps.cmd: sudo cp /etc/nginx/sites-available/host{,.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)} && sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx

steps.do: Check whether sites-enabled is a symlink or a real file before you 'fix' anything — replacing a symlink with a copy silently swaps the live config

pitfalls: An unmatched /api/* proxied to a workflow tool answers 200 with HTML; a frontend doing res.json() fails silently and you debug the wrong layer.
Renaming or copying the sites-available file can replace a symlink with a stale copy — the 'edits vanished' symptom.
Every new API path needs its own location block; relying on a generic /api/ prefix means the next service silently inherits the catch-all.
server_name changes do not move routes: the location list is what decides.
verify: Every owned path returns its own status from the origin (402/200 JSON, never an HTML fallback)
nginx -t is clean and the service is running after reload

items.title: How this bundle endpoint works (the mechanism you are calling)
items.solves: You are paying for one call and receiving a document set. This item explains the mechanism so you can build the same kind of product.
prerequisites: The x402 gate from the first playbook

steps.do: Keep the CONTENT in a JSON file next to the service, not in the code: content edits then need no code review and survive refactors
Serve a free listing on GET (ids + titles + price) and gate only POST, so agents can see what they would buy before paying
Support topic=<item id> to return a single playbook and format=markdown for one document — a caller pays once and gets exactly what it needs
Price per route rather than uniformly: data calls are cents, a multi-item knowledge bundle is dollars
Return provenance in the payload: bundle version, generated timestamp, item count, and the licence — the buyer can cite it
Register it like any other resource, then take one real payment to trigger indexing

pitfalls: Do not put content in the Python file if a non-developer might edit it; and do not fetch it from a third party at request time (latency plus an outage you cannot control).
A bundle is judged by its specificity. Generic advice is worthless next to the measured RPC table, the payload shapes and the pitfalls that cost real money.
If you filter by topic, keep the free listing in sync with the file or agents will pay for an id that returns nothing.
verify: GET returns the item list without a payment header
An unpaid POST returns 402 quoting the bundle price
A paid POST returns every item (or exactly the requested topic) with the settlement header present

items.title: Wire alerts and watchdog jobs to Telegram without leaking a bot token
items.solves: You want a cron job or a watchdog to tell you when something breaks, from a headless server, with credentials that never appear in code, chat or git.
prerequisites: A Telegram bot token from BotFather
A chat id
curl or Python on the host

steps.do: Create the bot with BotFather, then find the chat id by calling getUpdates after sending the bot one message
Store token and chat id in a mode-600 env file and load it at run time; never inline them in the script
Keep the sender tiny: read the env, build the message, POST it, and exit non-zero on failure so cron reports it
Make watchdogs idempotent: a marker file or a last-run timestamp so a persistent outage does not spam every interval
Have the job report the ARTIFACT, not a promise — the file path, the byte count, the exit code

pitfalls: A token pasted into a script eventually reaches a log, a git history or a screenshot. File + chmod 600 + env load is the whole point.
Telegram rate-limits: a loop that alerts every minute gets muted exactly when you need it.
Cron has a minimal environment — load the env file inside the script instead of relying on the shell profile.
'Job scheduled' is not 'job works'. Trigger it once manually and confirm the message arrived before trusting the schedule.
verify: A manual run delivers a message and exits 0
The token file is mode 600 and no token string appears in the repository
